data.content_ref: inline:The isolated problem 0e26d6be54fd depends on the basin-report mechanism (SRC_009): repertoire exhaustion and refuted-attractor dynamics explain WHY an artifact becomes isolated — the conjecture operator repeatedly proposes candidates that are refuted, collapsing into a basin where no surviving candidate bridges the artifact to its neighbourhood. The isolation is not a property of the artifact itself but of the conjecture-criticism loop's trajectory through candidate space. REFUTED IF: isolated artifacts can be connected without any change to the conjecture repertoire or candidate-generation strategy (i.e., the isolation is purely a retrieval/indexing failure, not a generative-attractor failure).
